learning_outcomes.text: Know about the advantages of using electric drives.
Know the principles of speed control DC motors, induction motors and brushless AC motors
Know the power electronic converter topologies used for speed control of DC motors, induction motors and brushless AC motors, and to be able to analyze these converters.
Can perform modeling and simulation analysis of dc motors.
Can design a simple controller for dc motors

syllabus_topics: Basic concepts of electric drives. Definition of a drive system and its components. Motors, power converters, semiconductor devices, gears and controllers.
Review of DC motors. Steady state and dynamic analysis of separately excited and PM dc motors.
Modeling of dc motors with state variables. Transfer functions. Control through armature and field circuits.
Phase Controlled DC Motor Drives: Principles and topologies
Chopper Controlled DC Motor Drives: Principles and topologies.
Designing a controller for PM dc motors.
Review and speed control principles of induction motors.
Inverter topologies: 6-step and PWM inverter operation.
Review and speed control principles of synchronous motors
Brushless DC and PM AC motors and drive principles.
bibliography: N. Mohan, Electric Drives: An Integrative Approach, Univ. of Minnesota Pr.
T. Wildi, Electrical Machines, Drives and Power Systems, Prentice Hall
R. Krishnan, Electric Motor Drives, Prentice Hall,2002
